1.q: What is the maximum PM Surya Ghar subsidy?
1.a: For eligible residential rooftop systems of 3 kW and above, the highlighted subsidy is up to ₹78,000 (1 kW ₹30,000; 2 kW ₹60,000). Final amount depends on government policy and approval.

2.a: Typically Aadhaar, PAN, latest electricity bill, and bank account details. We help you prepare the full file.

3.a: Nationalised bank solar loans are promoted at around 6% annual interest in our campaigns. Actual rates and eligibility depend on the bank.

4.a: Panel warranties are commonly up to 25 years; inverter warranties are often up to 2 years, depending on brand and terms.

commercialPage.title: Solar energy for businesses and industries
commercialPage.intro: Amma Solar helps commercial and industrial consumers across Maharashtra adopt solar for long-term economy — lower bills, stronger energy security, and clearer project economics.
commercialPage.vendor: Authorised vendor of MSEDCL for Maharashtra state. We support installation in any city across Maharashtra.

1.title: Lower operating costs
1.desc: Offset high commercial/industrial tariffs with daytime solar generation.

2.title: Predictable energy spend
2.desc: Reduce exposure to rising grid tariffs over 20+ years of plant life.

3.title: ESG & brand value
3.desc: Demonstrate clean energy commitment to customers and auditors.

4.title: RPO / compliance support
4.desc: Help larger HT/EHT consumers plan renewable purchase obligations where applicable.

commercialPage.financeIntro: Unlike residential PM Surya Ghar, commercial and industrial connections generally do not receive central capital subsidy (CFA). Savings come from policy incentives, tax treatment, net metering / open access, and financing. Always verify current MERC/MSEDCL/MNRE rules before committing.
commercialPage.noCfaTitle: Important: no PM Surya Ghar CFA for C&I
commercialPage.noCfaBody: Central Financial Assistance under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana is for residential (domestic) consumers. Commercial and industrial tariff categories are not eligible for that capital subsidy.

1.title: Accelerated depreciation
1.desc: Businesses can typically claim accelerated depreciation on solar assets (commonly cited around 40% in year one under current Income Tax rules for eligible plant — confirm with your CA).

2.title: Bank / NBFC project finance
2.desc: Term loans and green financing products from banks and NBFCs for rooftop and captive C&I solar; rates and tenure depend on credit profile.

3.title: RESCO / OPEX models
3.desc: Third-party ownership models can reduce upfront CapEx — power purchase at agreed tariffs (structure subject to regulation and contracts).

4.title: ALMM / quality compliance
4.desc: MNRE ALMM-listed modules and compliant design improve bankability and DISCOM acceptance.

1.title: MSEDCL net metering
1.desc: Eligible C&I consumers can apply for grid-interactive rooftop solar with net metering / related metering arrangements under MERC regulations via MSEDCL processes.

2.title: Electricity duty relief (policy-linked)
2.desc: Maharashtra renewable energy / storage policy frameworks have promoted duty exemptions for certain captive / BESS-linked projects (e.g. multi-year duty holidays where conditions are met). Eligibility is project-specific.

3.title: Green Energy Open Access
3.desc: Consumers meeting contract-demand thresholds (commonly 100 kW+) may explore green open access; banking and charges follow MERC rules and change over time.

4.title: Grid support / ToD banking rules
4.desc: MERC orders may apply grid support charges above certain sizes and time-of-day banking rules for non-residential consumers. We model these into project economics.

5.title: RPO for large consumers
5.desc: Covered HT/EHT consumers may have renewable purchase obligations — onsite or contracted solar can support compliance planning.

commercialPage.contactBody: Please email your unit location, sanctioned load / monthly bill, and roof or land details. We will respond with a project consultation.
